Triage: lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` (`resolvePasswordChangeUserId` at :4399 falls back to the bearer-derived principal when `getSessionFromCtx` yields nothing) → `domain:identity`, queued. Re-laned from `domain:auth` — not a lane-table label. Type intent: **Bug** (`type` field not set — `list_issue_types` 403 for this credential).

Added `security`: the same missing stash silently skips the ADR-0069 D1 password-reuse rejection and history recording on the bearer lane — a control enforced on one transport and absent on the other, with pins exercising only the working lane.

**`target:v17`** (classes ① + ②): every admin-provisioned API-lane user is permanently locked out with a 200 telling them the escape hatch worked (user-hit-today on the documented API lane), and a declared security control is unenforced per transport.

Acceptance shape endorsed as filed: both-transport test asserting the same post-conditions (`must_change_password === false`, `password_changed_at` stamped, history appended, protected read 200). Serial constraint: same package as in-flight #7735 (`plugin-auth`) — same-package rule says not the same batch; #7735's surface is the route ledger / better-auth config, this card is `auth-manager.ts`, so cross-check file surfaces at claim time and serialize if in doubt.

Size/model suggestion: M, `opus`.

Domain: `domain:identity`
File surface: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` — `resolvePasswordChangeUserId` (the `getSessionFromCtx` resolution, ~`:4399`), the `/change-password` after-hook (~`:1452`), and `stampPasswordChangedAt` (~`:4362`) — plus tests and a changeset.
Container & model: **M**, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — the fix is small, but it restores a **security control** (ADR-0069 D1 password-reuse rejection) that is currently transport-dependent, and the acceptance shape is a judgement call.
Serial constraints cleared: **`plugin-auth` is now free.** PR #8017 (#7735) **MERGED** — verified by content on `origin/main`: `changeEmail` enabled at `auth-manager.ts:975`, `user.deleteUser` still unconfigured (zero occurrences), ledger row `disposition: 'disabled'`. ⚠️ #7994 also lands in this package and is **held behind this card**.

## Why this ranks above the rest of the queue

`target:v17`, `bug`, `security`, and the filer measured **both transports** rather than one: cookie lane clears `must_change_password` and stamps `password_changed_at`; bearer lane answers **200**, really rotates the password, and clears nothing — so the caller is locked out of every protected route by a success response. The console is fine, which is exactly why this survived: every pin exercises the working lane.

## The half that is easy to under-fix, and is the reason this is `security`

The card names it and I am carrying it into the dispatch as non-negotiable: the **same** `__osPwChangeUserId` stash gates ADR-0069 D1's password-reuse rejection and the history append. On the bearer lane neither runs, so **password history is neither checked nor recorded**. A fix that only clears `must_change_password` makes the symptom disappear and leaves a security control silently absent on one transport — the worse residue, because the lockout at least announced itself.

> *"A control that is enforced on one transport and silently absent on the other is worse than one that is absent on both, because the pins and the console both exercise the working lane."*

## Premise re-verification is the dev's first action

The card was filed 13:38Z today against framework `279ee48a`, and `main` has taken merges since — including this lane's #8017, which touched **this very file**. The dev re-measures both lanes on current `origin/main` before editing. The filer's suggested shape (resolve the acting principal the way the rest of the pipeline already does, rather than adding a second stamp site) is explicitly labelled *not prescriptive* on the card, and I am passing it through as a suggestion, not a ruling.

**PM review: ACCEPT** — PR #8101. Seat #6022, session `session_01PEVB6w7D7uCszR9Mw1BL73`. CI convergence is mine.

## Verified against GitHub, not against the report

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| Path face — `docs/adr/**` / `.claude/skills/**` / `skills/**` | ✅ zero hits |
| Diff scope | ✅ exactly 3 files — `auth-manager.ts`, the new dogfood gate, the changeset |
| Edit 1 — `/change-password` routes through `resolveActor` | ✅ the bare `getSessionFromCtx` import is **deleted**, not shadowed |
| Edit 2 — signature stripped on **both** resolver branches | ✅ `const unsigned = (v: string) => v.split('.')[0]`, replacing the cookie-only strip |
| First line `Fixes #8049` | ✅ |

## The correction is the whole value of this run, and it would not have survived a lighter process

You did what the ruling asked — route `/change-password` through the pipeline's canonical resolver — and then **kept measuring instead of stopping there**. The result:

> `resolveActor`'s bearer branch looked the credential up **verbatim**, while its cookie branch stripped the signature — and `bearer()` issues the **signed** `token.signature` form in `set-auth-token`, which is the credential the card's own reproduction step 2 uses, while `sys_session.token` stores the unsigned value.

So the obvious, ruling-compliant, review-passing fix **leaves the documented lane fully broken** — and it leaves it broken in the way that is hardest to notice, because the unsigned spelling works and the test suite would have looked healthy. Ablation B is what proves both edits are load-bearing: removing only the normalization fails **3 tests, confined to the signed bearer lane**, exactly as predicted.

⚠️ **This is the second time today a card's obvious fix would have shipped a half-repair that passed its own acceptance criteria** (#8023's was placement, this one is credential shape). Both were caught by ablation, neither by review. That is the argument for keeping predict-then-mutate mandatory, restated with evidence.

## The `passwordHistoryCount` trap is the same class as #8074, one day later

> `passwordHistoryCount` defaults to **0 (off)** — which would have made every reuse assertion **vacuously green** — so the suite arms it to 3 through `applyConfigPatch`.

A reuse-rejection pin against a build where history is disabled passes for the wrong reason and certifies an untested control. That is precisely the failure mode #8074 was filed about this afternoon (an org-less fixture recording a real defect as passing), arriving independently in a different subsystem. Two instances in one shift is a pattern, and I have added it to #8074 as a second data point rather than letting it live only in this PR body.

## The docs question — checked, and no change needed

The drift check flagged `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`, and I said at dispatch time I'd read it rather than assume. Lines 788–789:

> While `mustChangePassword` is set, the user is blocked with `403 PASSWORD_EXPIRED` on every protected route **until they complete a password change**.

The prose is **transport-neutral and describes the intended behaviour** — which means it has been *accidentally false on the bearer lane* for as long as this bug existed, and your fix makes it true rather than requiring it to be rewritten. Same shape as #7807 an hour ago: the documentation was right and the runtime was lying. ⛔ No docs card.

## The `/sso/register` side effect — accepted, and I want it named in the changeset if it isn't

You stated it rather than hiding it: the same normalization repairs the `/sso/register` admin gate, which shares the resolver. Accepted, and the direction is what makes it safe — a gate that could not resolve a signed-bearer actor now can, so it **starts enforcing** where it previously did not. That is a narrowing, consistent with the card, and the honest place for a reader to meet it is the changeset.

## #8102 — filed correctly, and the `Blocked-by` is the right call

An inline copy of the same un-normalized token lookup at the D5.1 `/oauth2/authorize` gate, which is **fail-open for an unresolved actor** — same defect class, one endpoint over, and worse consequences. Two things you got right that are easy to get wrong: you set `Blocked-by: #8049` because the clean fix is to delete the copy and call `resolveActor`, which only becomes correct once this PR lands; and you **declined to grade the severity** because you read the code path and measured the token shapes but never drove a live bearer request at it. ⛔ Grading is the triage seat's channel, and an ungraded honest finding beats a confidently wrong one.

The two non-blocking notes (GitHub's duplicated attribution footer; the pre-existing plugin-auth TEST_DEBT gap of 23, tracked under #6376 and not moved here) are correctly left alone.

## Next steps (mine)

Read the per-job gate conclusions, then flip ready → arm, in that order. Then drive to MERGED and verify landing **content** on `origin/main`, including the negative space: that both branches still strip, and that the cookie lane's post-conditions are unchanged.

**MERGED and landing-verified** — PR #8101 landed as `36c2f002d`. Seat #6022. Card closed out.

Verified by **content on `origin/main`**, all three claims:

| claim | reading |
|:--|:--|
| 1. `/change-password` resolves through `resolveActor` | ✅ `resolvePasswordChangeUserId:4477` → for `/change-password`, `return (await this.resolveActor(ctx))?.userId` (`:4479`) |
| 2. the bare `getSessionFromCtx` is gone from that path | ✅ — see the caveat below |
| 3. **both** resolver branches strip the signature | ✅ `:3832` `const unsigned = (v) => v.split('.')[0]`, applied to the **bearer** branch (`:3834`) *and* the **cookie** branch (`:3837`) |

⚠️ **Claim 2 needed care, and it is the second time today a bare count nearly misled me.** `getSessionFromCtx` still returns **8 occurrences** in that file. That neither proves nor disproves the claim — other paths legitimately use it, and the claim was only ever about the `/change-password` branch. A count is not a verification; I read the specific site, and there the bare call is genuinely replaced.

Had I stopped at "8, not 0" I would have raised a false alarm — the mirror image of the "1, not 0" reading on #8023 that turned out to be an unrelated comment. **Both directions of that mistake are available, and only reading the hit settles it.**

**Item 3 is the one worth naming again**: it is the half your ablation B proved load-bearing, and the half a future refactor is most likely to "simplify" back into a cookie-only strip. It is now pinned by your both-transports gate, so a regression there fails loudly instead of silently restoring the bug on the documented lane.

`plugin-auth` is now free. #7994 is being claimed next; #8102's `Blocked-by: #8049` is also cleared by this landing, but that card is ungraded and belongs to the triage seat's channel — ⛔ not claimed here.
